To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the physiological stimulator of pentose phosphate pathway activity, pyrroline carboxylate (P5C) increases the generation of 5-phospho-D-ribosyl-1- pyrophosphate (PRP) in mouse liver in vitro and in vivo.

P5C, a physiological stimulator, increases the hepatic content of ribose- 5-phosphate and of PRPP and that this effect provides evidence for a regulatory effect of R5P on PRPP generation and nucleotide production.
the stimulation of PRPRP generation by P5c also occurs in liver, and that it is accompanied by a smaller and transient elevation in R5P content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the physiological role of the P5C-induced stimulation of the pentose-phosphate pathway in nucleotide synthesis.
the regulation of nucleotide synthesis by R5P.
the regulation of purine nucleotide synthesis in the cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the physiological role of P5C is to increase the flux of R5P through the ribulose-phosphate pathway, thus stimulating purine synthesis and increasing the availability of PRPP for the synthesis of pyrimidines and other nucleotides.

the P5C-mediated increase in the rate of R5P generation in the hexose-monophosphopentose pathway is responsible for the stimulation of PRP generation, and thus nucleotide synthesis, in mouse liver in the presence of a physiological stimulator.
P5C is a physiological stimulator for the generation of R5P and its subsequent conversion to PRPP and nucleotides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stimulation of PRRP and nucleotide synthesis by P5C is due to an increase in R5P availability, which is caused by an elevation in the R5P-generating capacity of the pentose-phosphate pathway.
R5P is an important regulatory metabolite in the control of purine nucleotide synthesis in the liver and in erythrocytes.
P5C stimulates nucleotide synthesis through the stimulation of R5P and subsequent PRPP generation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of PRP generation by R5P availability may represent a novel mechanism of purine nucleotide homeostasis.
P5C is a potent physiological stimulator of PRPP generation and nucleotide biosynthesis in vivo, and that this effect is mediated by R5P availability.
P5C can serve as a useful tool for studying the regulatory mechanisms of the pentose phosphate pathway in vivo.
